ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a simple atomic skeleton arrangement, with the letter S located in the upper middle, and three O distributed around it: one O at the upper left, one O at the upper right, and one O in the lower middle. From this it can be known that S should be taken as the central atom, and the three O should be connected to S to construct the Lewis structure of SO3^2−. Reasoning: The number of valence electrons of SO3^2− is S's 6, plus the 18 of the three O, plus the 2 brought by the 2− charge, for a total of 26 valence electrons. First place three S−O single bonds, using 6 electrons; then complete the octets of the three oxygen atoms, using 18 electrons; the remaining 2 electrons serve as one lone pair on the sulfur atom. If all are single bonds, the three oxygens each carry −1, sulfur carries +1, and the formal charges are not minimized. To minimize formal charges, convert one lone pair of one oxygen into an S=O double bond, obtaining one S=O and two S−O−, with sulfur still having one lone pair; the double-bond position can resonate among the three oxygens. In this way sulfur has three bonding regions and one lone pair around it, therefore the molecular/ion geometry is trigonal pyramidal, not trigonal planar. Because the trigonal pyramidal shape is asymmetric, the S−O bond dipoles cannot completely cancel, so sulfite ion is polar. Therefore, the incorrect statement is: sulfite ion is nonpolar.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the skeleton shows S as the central atom with three O atoms positioned around it, so construct a sulfite ion Lewis structure with sulfur bonded to all three oxygens. From the text, note that formal charges should be minimized and the target is the incorrect statement about sulfite. Count 26 valence electrons for SO3^2−, place three S−O bonds, complete O octets, then use remaining electrons to give sulfur one lone pair. Minimize formal charges by converting one O lone pair into an S=O double bond, leaving two singly bonded O atoms with −1 charges and resonance among equivalent positions. Determine the shape around sulfur: three bonds plus one lone pair make the ion trigonal pyramidal rather than trigonal planar. Because this shape is asymmetric and the S−O bond dipoles do not cancel, the sulfite ion is polar. Therefore the incorrect statement is: “The sulfite ion is nonpolar.”
